reason: E1 shows a 3× TBR reduction via nanoscale trenches for GaN/diamond, supporting the contact-area premise, but it does not involve HEAs, W, or CuCrZr, so the transferability premise is unsupported. No evidence is cited for the HEA's mechanical stability after nanopatterning or the feasibility of patterning this specific alloy.
premises: Nanoscale trenches can reduce effective thermal boundary resistance (TBR) by increasing contact area.
The TBR reduction mechanism demonstrated for GaN/diamond interfaces is transferable to (CrFeTiTa)70W30 HEA interfaces.
Nanopatterning will not degrade the bulk microstructure or mechanical integrity of the HEA.
The proposed FIB/plasma nanopatterning can create the specified trench dimensions on the HEA surface.
